summary: Established an AIDE-based integrity baseline for /etc on node1 (Ubuntu 24.04): installed aide/aide-common, configured /etc/aide/aide.conf to recursively track /etc with a full attribute+hash ruleset (permissions, ownership, size, mtime/ctime, md5+sha256+acl+xattrs), initialized the database at /var/lib/aide/aide.db (1950 entries), and verified detection works by creating/removing canary files in /etc (AIDE correctly flagged the additions and the resulting /etc directory mtime change), then re-initialized a clean baseline afterward. Confirmed a clean check. Completed the mandatory single-node restart protocol: captured boot_id/btime/uptime and a clean AIDE check as pre-restart baseline, issued shutdown -r now with acknowledgement returned before disconnect, polled until node1 was reachable again, confirmed boot_id changed (a0c36ad2-af0d-42fe-ad6f-4750699390c2 -> fc0eb3ab-0761-4bb6-90dc-8bd5447f49e8) and btime advanced (1790687964 -> 1790688074) with fresh uptime (~6.5s), and verified post-restart that the AIDE database is byte-identical (same SHA256 d536d0b5...) and /etc still checks clean against the baseline.
actions_performed: Inspected node1 OS and captured pre-change boot_id
Installed aide and aide-common packages via apt
Wrote a scoped /etc/aide/aide.conf with a full-attribute rule applied recursively to /etc
Initialized the AIDE database (1950 entries) and installed it as the active baseline at /var/lib/aide/aide.db, recording creation timestamp and SHA256 checksum
Falsification test: created canary files under /etc and confirmed AIDE --check flagged them as added/changed entries
Reverted the canary files and re-initialized a clean baseline reflecting the true intended state
Confirmed a clean AIDE check (no differences) prior to restart
Captured pre-restart boot identity (boot_id, btime, uptime) and AIDE db checksum
Issued sudo -n shutdown -r now in the background with a returned acknowledgement before disconnection
Polled node1 until exec access returned
Confirmed changed boot_id/btime/uptime proving a genuine restart occurred
Verified post-restart the AIDE database file is unchanged (identical SHA256) and a fresh --check reports no differences from the /etc baseline

evidence.summary: AIDE installed, /etc/aide/aide.conf scoped to /etc with full attribute+hash rule, database initialized with 1950 entries, installed as /var/lib/aide/aide.db, and initial --check reports 'AIDE found NO differences between database and filesystem. Looks okay!!'

evidence.requirement: Baseline correctly detects changes to /etc (falsification proof)
evidence.summary: Canary files added under /etc were flagged by AIDE as 3 added entries; after cleanup, AIDE still correctly flagged the /etc directory's changed mtime/ctime, proving the detection mechanism is sensitive and functioning

evidence.requirement: Clean baseline re-established and confirmed before restart
evidence.summary: Database re-initialized after test cleanup (1950 entries), checksum d536d0b5... recorded, and --check reports clean; pre-restart snapshot also captured boot_id a0c36ad2... and btime 1790687964
Captured boot_id, btime, uptime, AIDE db SHA256, and a clean AIDE check immediately before initiating reboot

evidence.requirement: Mandatory restart: acknowledgement returned before disconnect
evidence.summary: shutdown -r now issued in background; 'issuing reboot' acknowledgement printed before the exec stream closed due to the node going down

evidence.requirement: Mandatory restart: node down then reachable again
evidence.summary: Connection reset confirmed node was down; subsequent poll succeeded once node1 came back up

evidence.requirement: Mandatory restart: changed boot identity proven
evidence.summary: boot_id changed from a0c36ad2-af0d-42fe-ad6f-4750699390c2 to fc0eb3ab-0761-4bb6-90dc-8bd5447f49e8, btime advanced from 1790687964 to 1790688074, and uptime reset to ~6.5s

evidence.requirement: Mandatory restart: post-restart recovery of required data verified
evidence.summary: Post-restart, /var/lib/aide/aide.db is present with identical SHA256 (d536d0b5...) to the pre-restart baseline, and a fresh AIDE --check reports 'Looks okay!!' with the same 1950 entries, confirming the integrity baseline survived the restart intact
